back2basics.text: Candidates contesting elections must file affidavits disclosing personal details like assets and criminal records to ensure transparency. The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs these disclosures and penalizes false information to maintain election integrity. The judiciary interprets these laws to balance citizen rights and electoral fairness.

2026-10-24-am-1cacf6e8cb.deck: The Supreme Court ruled that private citizens can file criminal complaints against electoral candidates who provide false or conceal information in nomination papers. This judgment enhances electoral transparency and accountability, a key topic for understanding the judiciary's role in governance.

body.label: Voters' legal standing
body.text: The Court held that ordinary private citizens, not only public servants or authorities, can file criminal complaints against candidates for false or concealed information in nomination papers.

body.label: Scope of Section 125-A
body.text: Section 125-A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, penalizes false affidavits with imprisonment up to six months, fine, or both, and this section allows complaints by private persons.

body.label: Interpretation of Section 195 CrPC
body.text: The Court clarified that the restriction in Section 195 of the CrPC, which limits cognizance of offences to complaints by public servants, does not apply to Section 125-A of the 1951 Act.

Reserve money is the base money created by the central bank, while money supply includes currency and deposits circulating in the economy. Treasury bills are short-term government securities issued to meet temporary funding needs and manage public debt.

back2basics.concept: Forest Rights Act and Community Forest Resource Rights
back2basics.text: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, recognizes the rights of forest-dwelling communities over forest land and resources. It includes Individual Forest Rights (IFR) and Community Forest Resource Rights (CFRR), which empower communities to manage and conserve forests sustainably. The Act mandates Gram Sabha participation in claim recognition and aims to balance forest conservation with tribal livelihoods.

2026-10-24-am-3e86b02227.deck: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs held the Third Regional Review Conference in Srinagar on 23 October 2026 to assess the implementation of the Forest Rights Act across seven States and UTs. This review focused on pending claims, community forest resource rights, and livelihood convergence, emphasizing time-bound action plans, which is crucial for understanding tribal rights and forest governance in India.

editor.prelimsAngle: Forest Rights Act provisions and implementation.
editor.why: Forest Rights Act implementation is key to tribal rights and environmental governance.

mains.demand: Explain how review conferences aid in addressing challenges and improving the implementation of the Forest Rights Act for tribal welfare and sustainable forest management.
mains.question: Discuss the significance of the Forest Rights Act implementation review conferences in strengthening tribal rights and forest governance in India.

body: Review conferences provide a platform for States and UTs to share progress, challenges, and best practices in claim disposal and rights recognition.
They emphasize transparency, timely processing of claims, and stronger Gram Sabha participation, which are crucial for tribal empowerment.
The conferences promote convergence of forest rights with livelihood schemes and sustainable forest management through Community Forest Resource Rights.
They facilitate monitoring through State Level Monitoring Committees and encourage digitisation and integration of records for better governance.
structure.conclusion: Thus, these conferences play a vital role in ensuring effective implementation of the FRA, balancing tribal rights with conservation goals.
structure.intro: The Forest Rights Act aims to recognize and protect the rights of forest-dwelling communities, and review conferences assess its implementation.

mcq.trap: Statement 1 is correct as the conference included Maharashtra and Jammu & Kashmir among others; Statement 2 is correct with exact figures from the official data.

body.label: Review implementation progress
body.text: Senior officials from Maharashtra, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Rajasthan, and Jammu & Kashmir assessed the status of forest rights claims, community forest resource rights, and livelihood convergence.

body.label: Identify challenges and priorities
body.text: The conference discussed obstacles in claim disposal and emphasized the need for transparent, timely processes and stronger interdepartmental coordination.

body.label: Emphasize time-bound action plans
body.text: States were urged to prepare district-wise plans to expedite pending claims and review rejected cases, ensuring rights recognition advances alongside conservation and sustainable development.

sections.heading: What was the purpose of the Third Regional Review Conference on FRA?

body.label: Claims and titles statistics
body.text: As of 31 August 2026, about 54 lakh claims were received nationally, with 43.56 lakh disposed of, 25.42 lakh titles distributed over nearly 238 lakh acres, 10.45 lakh claims pending, and 18.13 lakh rejected.

body.label: Community Forest Resource Rights
body.text: Recognition and sustainable management of Community Forest Resource Rights (CFRR) were highlighted, with calls for convergence of CFR Management Plans with Forest Department Working Plans.

body.label: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
body.text: Habitat rights have been recognized for only 11 of the 75 PVTGs in India, and States were urged to expedite their recognition and develop PVTG-wise Habitat Rights roadmaps.

sections.heading: What is the current status of Forest Rights Act implementation?

body.label: Maharashtra's progress
body.text: Distributed 2,03,510 individual and 8,821 community titles; CFR rights cover about 13.87 lakh acres with 7,518 CFR Committees and 1,875 management plans.

body.label: Gujarat's efforts
body.text: Distributed 1,00,747 individual and 3,879 community titles; satellite verification and FRA Cells address pendency; PVTGs identified with a Habitat Rights Action Plan to be submitted.

body.label: Jammu & Kashmir's status
body.text: Received 48,287 claims, approved 6,191, and distributed 6,178 titles covering approximately 3,960 hectares, mainly community rights; has SLMC under Chief Secretary and directives to prevent eviction before due process.

body.label: Other States' updates
body.text: Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Goa, and Rajasthan have made varying progress in title distribution, record incorporation, and committee meetings, with ongoing efforts to resolve pending and rejected claims.

sections.heading: How are States progressing in FRA implementation?

body.label: District-wise action plans
body.text: States and UTs must prepare detailed plans identifying delays, responsible authorities, and stages of pending claims.

body.label: Review rejected claims
body.text: Rejections must be supported by reasoned orders with appeal rights preserved, and a one-time window to review rejected claims is suggested.

body.label: Digitisation and integration
body.text: Complete digitisation and incorporation of recognised rights into revenue and forest records are to be done as per the advisory dated 24 June 2026.

body.label: Capacity building and convergence
body.text: States should strengthen Gram Sabhas, raise awareness, provide post-claim support, facilitate CFR Management Plans, and align with livelihood and welfare schemes.

body.label: Monitoring and reporting
body.text: Quarterly reviews through State Level Monitoring Committees chaired by Chief Secretaries and regular submission of reconciled Monthly Progress Reports are mandated.

sections.heading: What are the key recommendations and next steps from the conference?

back2basics.text: Irrigation involves supplying water to agricultural fields to support crop growth, especially during dry seasons. Effective management is crucial for sustaining agricultural productivity and rural livelihoods.

2026-10-24-am-62998f9115.deck: Farmers in Karnataka's Vijayapura and Bagalkot districts oppose the state government's decision to withhold irrigation water from Almatti and Narayanpur reservoirs for the rabi season, threatening protests. Automatic withholding of payments until verification safeguards public funds and protects workers' wages.

body.label: Liveness detection and anti-tampering
body.text: The upgraded app includes AI-based liveness detection to verify that the person is a live worker, preventing use of dummy images or old photos.

body.label: Enhanced face verification

body.label: Photo de-duplication module
body.text: An AI module identifies suspicious or repeated photographs to detect fraudulent attendance entries.

body.label: Automatic withholding of payments
body.text: When suspicious entries are detected, wage lists and Fund Transfer Orders are automatically withheld until checks are completed.

body.text: Despite earlier face authentication, fake attendance was recorded using photo-to-photo capturing instead of live images.

body.label: Discrepancies detected
body.text: There were mismatches in worker counts, gender composition, repeated photos in multiple muster rolls, and inconsistencies between morning and afternoon attendance.

body.label: Protecting wages and public funds
body.text: The government aims to safeguard workers' wages and ensure public funds are transparently used for their intended purpose.

sections.heading: Why was the AI upgrade necessary?

body.label: Exception mechanism
body.text: Face authentication exceptions are allowed for elderly workers, persons with disabilities, or when technical issues occur.

sections.heading: How does the system handle offline and exceptional cases?

body.text: As of October 2026, 31.23 lakh worksites are active, employing over 3.65 crore workers from 2.89 crore rural households.

back2basics.text: Capital adequacy refers to the minimum capital a bank must hold to cover its risks and protect depositors. Operational risk involves losses from failures in internal processes, people, systems, or external events. Basel III norms set international standards for banks to maintain sufficient capital against such risks, ensuring financial stability.

2026-10-24-am-f52074e680.deck: The Reserve Bank of India issued the Second Amendment Directions, 2026, specifying the implementation of the Basel III Standardised Approach for operational risk capital requirements effective April 1, 2027. This update is crucial for understanding the evolving regulatory framework governing commercial banks' risk management.

body.label: New amendment issued
body.text: RBI issued the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Forthcoming Instructions) Second Amendment Directions, 2026, updating operational risk capital requirements.

body.label: Basel III Standardised Approach
body.text: The amendment specifies implementation of the Basel III Standardised Approach for minimum operational risk regulatory capital requirements.

body.label: Implementation date
body.text: The new norms will come into effect from April 1, 2027.

body.label: Scope of applicability
body.text: These directions apply to commercial banks excluding Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Regional Rural Banks.

body.label: Additional clarifications
body.text: The amendment incorporates further clarifications issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision after the initial 2025 Directions.

sections.heading: What changes did RBI make to operational risk capital requirements?

body.label: Risk management framework
body.text: The amendment reflects RBI's alignment with international Basel III norms, strengthening banks' capital buffers against operational risks.

body.label: Financial stability
body.text: By updating capital requirements, RBI aims to enhance the resilience of commercial banks to operational losses.

body.label: Exam relevance
body.text: Understanding RBI's regulatory updates on capital adequacy is important for questions on financial sector regulation and risk management.

sections.heading: Why does this matter for banking regulation and exams?

body.label: Leverage ratio update
body.text: On the same day, RBI also issued final guidelines on implementing the Leverage Ratio 2017 Standard, effective April 1, 2027.

body.label: Comprehensive capital norms
body.text: These concurrent updates indicate RBI's comprehensive approach to revising prudential norms for capital adequacy.
